title: Why Honey Never Spoils
credits: Facts: Smithsonian Magazine, "The Science Behind Honey's Eternal Shelf Life" (2013)

scenes.say: Archaeologists found honey in Egyptian tombs. Three thousand years old, and still edible.
scenes.visual: Fig. 1 honey jar drawn on; 3,000 years counter on 'thousand'; 'edible' underlined in red

scenes.say: Honey is mostly sugar with barely any water, so it pulls the water out of germs.
scenes.visual: bar: sugar ~80% vs water ~17%; arrows pull drops out of a microbe on 'germs'

scenes.say: It's acidic too, close to orange juice.
scenes.visual: pH scale, marker slides to about 3.9 on 'acidic'; orange slice drawn beside on 'orange'

scenes.say: And bees add an enzyme that makes hydrogen peroxide.
scenes.visual: bee drawn on 'bees'; H2O2 label fades in on 'peroxide'

scenes.say: Keep it sealed, and almost nothing can grow in it.
scenes.visual: jar lid drawn on 'sealed'; round seal 'Never spoils' on 'nothing'
